chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya and others, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hamid, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) judged regarding the one who severely punished his slave, that he was free, there being no way for him (the master) against him (the slave), being unconditionally freed, he can go and give his guardianship to whoever he so likes to. So when he is responsible for his crimes, so he would inherit him.

key_terms.جَرِيرَتَهُ: His crime or fault (specifically regarding blood money/diyah)
key_terms.سَائِبَةٌ: Unconditionally freed slave (who is not bound to a specific guardian by choice or debt)

ai.seo_question: What is the legal status and inheritance rule of a slave freed due to severe punishment (Saibah)?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the status of the 'Saibah'—a slave unconditionally freed due to the master's severe punishment—establishing that the master retains inheritance rights only if he guarantees the slave's blood money (diyah) for any crimes committed. This ruling highlights the unique Shia jurisprudential view where the master's liability for the freed slave's actions creates a reciprocal inheritance bond, distinguishing it from other forms of manumission. It underscores the principle that freedom from bondage does not sever all legal ties, particularly regarding financial accountability in the context of tribal and family law.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya and someone else, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Hameed, from Hisham Bin Saalim, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>

having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> judged regarding the one severely punished his slave, that he was free, there being no way for him (the master) against him (the slave), being unconditionally freed, he can go and give his guardianship to whoever he so likes to. So when he is responsible for his crimes, so he would inherit him’.
en.sarwar: 9. Muhammad ibn Yahya and others have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Hamid from Hisham ibn Salim from abu Basir who has narrated the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

Amir al-Mu’minin once issued a judgment. It was in the case of a slave whose master had caused him serious physical damage, that he (the slave) is free in the manner of Sa’ibah (unconditionally freed slave) so that he can choose whomever he likes as his guardian to bail out his liabilities for his crimes and then inherit his legacy.”’
